title: Every fixed Krylov degree gives a strictly stronger variational and scalar-recentering boundary

variational_hierarchy.coefficients: Let epsilon_d be K1494's uniform strict gap and define c_1=1, c_d=1+sum_(r=2)^d epsilon_r. Then c_d is strictly increasing in every finite d
variational_hierarchy.multiplication_bottom: K1484 gives lambda_min(J_(1,N))=-1+o(1), while K1494 gives lambda_min(J_(d,N))<=-c_d+o(1) for every fixed d
variational_hierarchy.free_cost: The degree-d polynomial Krylov space lies in Wiener degree at most 4d and cutoff frequencies at most N, so every normalized vector in it has H0 form value at most 4d omega_max(N)=O_d(N)
variational_hierarchy.ground_energy_upper: For every fixed d and g>0, E_N<=6gC_N^2-c_d g sigma_N+O_d(N)
variational_hierarchy.necessary_recentering: Uniform semiboundedness of H_N-a_N therefore requires a_N<=6gC_N^2-c_d g sigma_N+O_d(N) for every fixed d
variational_hierarchy.explicit_divergent_window: For fixed d and delta>0, any eventual a_N>=6gC_N^2-g(c_d-delta)sigma_N has inf spec(H_N-a_N)<=-g delta sigma_N+O_d(N)->-infinity
variational_hierarchy.ceiling: This is a family of one-sided fixed-degree upper bounds. It neither proves sup_d c_d=infinity nor supplies a matching lower bound, a weakly convergent trial family, Mosco recovery, ground-state compactness or a common nonlinear continuum domain
